title: Cross-product cadence orchestration matrix for runtime/console/api launches
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Create an operational 'Cadence Orchestration Matrix' and playbook that maps product roadmaps, cycle milestones, and OKR checkpoints into a single launch calendar for runtime, console, and API surface launches. This artifact should drive deterministic release windows, clearly owned gating criteria, and an automated calendar feed that downstream teams (support, sales, SRE) can subscribe to.

Why now: As we scale Dedicated and Private deployments and increase cadence of runtime improvements (kernel updates, batching), coordination friction has increased. Multiple teams are independently picking launch dates which leads to conflicting rollout windows, missed canary syncs, and unclear owner handoffs for observability/config changes.

Scope and deliverables:
- Cadence Orchestration Matrix (CSV/Sheet) that lists: launch owner, product area (runtime/console/api), target cycle, semantic risk level, dependency keys, gating criteria, canary rollout plan (percentages + regions), rollback criteria, and required artifacts (docs, SDKs, migration guides).
- Playbook (Confluence) with step-by-step coordination steps for pre-launch, canary validation, ramp, and post-launch validation tied to specific SLOs and cost deltas.
- Automated calendar integration (Google Calendar + iCal) and a read-only dashboard view in Console showing upcoming launches and critical flags.
- Template PR for release notes and a checklist that must be completed before a launch goes from 'Planned' -> 'Scheduled'.

Acceptance philosophy: The matrix must reduce ambiguity — each row has a single named owner, explicit gating criteria that are either pass/fail or measurable, and a dependency list that is actionable. Playbook must include at least two runbooks for rollback cases (runtime regression, console outage) and an SLO verification checklist.

Out-of-scope: Detailed rollout automation (CI/CD pipelines) and automated canary gating rules; those are engineering deliverables referenced as dependencies.
comments: 2026-02-24 - Kickoff: Alignment with Eng and Design. Agreed to prioritize canonical matrix first, then calendar automation. Attendees: Maya Chen (PM), Liam O'Connor (PM owner), Priya Rao (Eng manager), Sven Müller (Runtime lead), Ana Ruiz (Console PM), Ravi Patel (SRE).

2026-03-02 - Draft matrix prototype uploaded to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1exampleMatrix. Feedback: runtime wants an explicit field for 'kernel/quantization change' and a 'sequence length impact' note. Console requests a column for 'dashboard rollout window' and support handoff slack channel.

2026-03-05 - Trade-off discussion: Tightening launch windows increases predictability but reduces flexibility for hotfixes. Decided to keep weekly 'soft windows' with hard gating criteria that can push to the next soft window without executive review. Logged in Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RELEASE/pages/12345-Cadence-Tradeoffs

2026-03-08 - Eng dependencies identified: ENG-4821 (canary metrics pipeline), ENG-4903 (runtime canary orchestration), ENG-5017 (console release notes automation). We will block scheduling until ENG-4821 is in 'In Review' for critical launches.

2026-03-10 - Preview to leadership (GTM and SRE): positive feedback; request to include a 'customer-impact classification' for each launch mapped to external comms templates. Action: add 'customer_impact' column and link to comms templates.

2026-03-12 - Pre-schedule review: matrix v0.3 attached to this ticket and a test calendar feed created (ics link). Assigned follow-ups: Liam to finalize playbook draft, Priya to confirm ENG-4821 timeline, Ana to create comms templates.
acceptance_criteria: Cadence Orchestration Matrix published to Drive with owner, gating criteria, and explicit dependencies for the next 6 cycles.
Playbook published in Confluence with runbooks for two rollback scenarios and SLO verification steps.
Calendar integration (Google Calendar / iCal) proof-of-concept created and accessible to cross-functional teams.
At least one pilot launch scheduled using the matrix (runtime kernel patch) and validated end-to-end: docs, canary, rollback test.
Dashboard tile in Console shows upcoming launches with status flags (green/amber/red).
risks: Engineering bandwidth for canary metric pipeline (ENG-4821) slips, preventing scheduling of high-risk runtime changes.
Lack of enforcement: teams ignore the playbook and continue ad-hoc launches, undermining the matrix's value.
Calendar integration leaks internal metadata if permissions are misconfigured (privacy/comms risk).
mitigations: Prioritize ENG-4821 as a critical dependency for high-risk launches; create a short-term manual metrics collection option for pilots.
Add a lightweight pre-schedule gating step in the Console where PMs must confirm checklist items before a launch is 'Scheduled'.
Use read-only calendar feeds and mask sensitive fields; add a review step for external-facing comms templates.
timeline: 2026-03-25 - Target: iterate based on pilot learnings and finalize automation backlog
